newsitem.title: USA: US Republican leaders see crucial talks on budget.
newsitem.headline: US Republican leaders see crucial talks on budget.

text.p: House and Senate Republican leaders said Tuesday the reopening this week of budget talks with the White House will be key towards reaching agreement on balancing the budget, and if no progress is made they are ready to work on a separate congressional budget.

Top White House officials were to meet the chairmen and senior Democrats on the House and Senate Budget Committees at 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) for the first in a series of meetings. "The White House should note, four to five solid days here might be enough, and then we will proceed on another front," Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici told reporters.

Domenici and House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich, both Republicans, said they were ready to work with moderate and conservative Democrats to craft a bipartisan budget proposal if they see no movement in talks with the administration.

Domenici stressed the importance of this week's talks. "I perceive that we are enter a new phase today, this afternoon. We will continue this discussions with high level representatives of the president through this week," the New Mexico Republican said.
"We hope we can reach an agreement with the president. If we can't we will have a strong proposal ourselves. We have been working on this for a long time," Kasich, an Ohio Republican, said.

House Speaker Newt Gingrich of Georgia, Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott and other top Republicans said they remain committed to enacting a tax cut this year as well as reining in government spending growth to bring the deficit to zero in five years.
The Republican leaders spoke to reporters after an hour-long closed-door meeting called to discuss the congressional agenda.
Lott reiterated Republican desires to provide tax relief for families and relief from estate taxes. "And, we are absolutely committed to capital gains tax rate cuts, the Mississippi Republican added.
